title: Going from Place to Place
editorial: Get an IC card such as Suica for supported local trains, subways, buses, and some purchases. It saves repeatedly buying tickets, but isn't a universal ticket for every service.

Tokyo's rail network did most of the work for us. In Kyoto, buses were often more useful for reaching our chosen sights, though bringing a large suitcase onto a packed bus was a miserable idea. Hiroshima's streetcars were straightforward; the flat fare we recorded was ¥240 at the time of our visit.
If an IC card reports an unfinished journey, ask station staff for help. We had an untapped ride fixed with some Google Translate.
Use the Shinkansen for Tokyo → Kyoto, Kyoto → Hiroshima, and Hiroshima → Osaka. Miyajima adds a mainland connection to Miyajimaguchi and a short ferry crossing.
Airport transfers need their own planning. Our Narita arrival involved a separate Skyliner ticket as well as the Suica card. Don't assume an IC card alone covers the whole airport journey.
Compare individual tickets with relevant rail passes for your actual route before buying. We haven't recorded enough ticket costs here to claim which option was cheapest.
Station coin lockers were useful. We paid ¥700 for a large locker, cheaper than the luggage-storage alternative we'd considered. Availability and sizes vary.
Cabs are where the budget can unravel. One 25-minute Kyoto ride cost us ¥4,300.
Transport references: JNTO — IC cards and Miyajima access.
